text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- CHRISTMAS SALES RISE SLIGHTLY
Christmas sales this year were good but not as strong as anticipated. As a result many retail outlets have excess inventory which will reduce demand from factories.
--IF RE-ELECTION FAILS, TASSO WILL BE THE ALTERNATIVE IN '98

Ceara state Gov. Tasso Jereissati has surfaced as the main alternative to lead the Social Democratic Party in 1998 presidential elections if President Fernando Henrique Cardoso fails in his bid to amend the constitution to allow re-election.
GOVERNMENT SEES GROWTH IN EXPORTS

The government's economic team sees many sectors of the economy improving next year, which should boost exports. Autos, textiles and petrochemicals are among the sectors expected to benefit by ongoing efforts to reduce port costs, increase export financing alternatives and ease foreign direct investment rules.
O GLOBO
-- BANERJ BANK AUCTION SUSPENDED FOR THE SECOND TIME

Hours before state development bank Banerj was to be auctioned off, a Rio de Janeiro judge ordered a re-evaluation of Banerj assets, forcing officials to postpone the auction for the second time in 10 days.
-- RAIN KILLS THREE IN NOVA FRIBURGO
Three people were killed and 200 were left homeless by heavy rain in the city of Nova Friburgo in Rio de Janeiro state.
-- TERRORISTS FREE GUATEMALAN HOSTAGE IN PERU
Rebels of Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement freed Guatemala's ambassador, reducing to 103 the number of hostages they are holding at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GOVERNMENT WANTS TO CHANGE CONCUBINE LAW

The government has sent Congress a bill to change the Concubine Law approved earlier this year. The new bill would create a Statute of Stable Union that requires non-married couples to be living together under the same roof for at least five years before they can legally be considered a couple. The existing law sets no minimum period.
-- BOMB EXPLODES AT JAPANESE AMBASSADOR'S HOUSE IN LIMA
A bomb exploded yesterday at the Japanese amabassador's residence in Lima, Peru, where rebels are holding more than 100 hostages.
-- LAWYER GROUP CAMPAIGNS FOR RE-ELECTION REFERENDUM
Brazil's Order of Attorney's will launch a campaign at the beginning of next year calling for a referendum to decide whether or not the country should permit re-election of executive office holders.
* Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--John Miller, Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 248-5414
